name: Forearm plank
summary: Hold your body in a straight line on your forearms and toes. Trains the trunk to resist sagging.
setup: Elbows directly under your shoulders, forearms parallel or hands lightly clasped.
Step your feet back, hip width apart, and come onto your toes.

steps.text: Push your forearms into the floor so your upper back rounds slightly between the shoulder blades.
Squeeze your glutes and tuck your pelvis, as if pulling your belt buckle up toward your chin. Your lower back flattens.
Hold a straight line from ears to ankles. Breathe slowly through the whole hold.

jointCues.cue: Spread apart: push the floor away. Do not sink between the shoulders.
jointCues.why: Sinking hangs your weight on the shoulder ligaments instead of the serratus and chest.

jointCues.cue: Under the shoulders. You can also pull them toward your toes without moving them.
jointCues.why: Elbows far ahead strain the shoulder; dragging them toward the toes makes the plank much harder for the abs.
This stops the lower back from sagging into an arch, the most common fault.

jointCues.cue: Long, eyes on the floor just ahead of your hands.
jointCues.why: Lifting the head strains the neck.

breathing: Breathe steadily through your nose: short breaths in, longer breaths out, without letting your belly or hips drop. Do not hold your breath.
tempo: Hold 20 to 60 s; stop when the line breaks

mistakes.fix: Squeeze glutes and tuck the pelvis. End the set when you cannot hold the line.
Lower them until ears, hips and ankles line up.
Count your breaths. Five slow breaths is a good first target.

cues.text: Push the floor away; shoulder blades spread apart
Ears, hips and ankles in one line; breathe slowly
